# Duck Inspector (ukr. Качиний Інспектор)
> Duck Inspector indexes Ukrainian archival records — a four-level hierarchy of
> archive → fond → inventory → file — and points to scans of those files hosted
> on other services (state archive portals, FamilySearch, Wikisource, etc.).
> Duck Inspector does not host the scans itself. This file documents the public,
> read-only JSON API for AI agents and other automated clients.

## Rate limit

**Important: keep requests to 5 per 10 seconds per client.** This is not
currently enforced by a hard server-side block, but clients that exceed it
consistently may be throttled or IP-blocked without notice. Duck Inspector is
a free, volunteer-run, ad-free project with no dedicated API infrastructure —
batch lookups where the endpoint allows it (e.g. one `/api/search` call with
filters) rather than looping over many small requests, and cache results
instead of re-fetching.

## Base URL

`https://inspector.duckarchive.com`

## Authentication

None. Every endpoint below is public and read-only. Do not attempt to send an
`Authorization` header — it is only used by unrelated, non-public account
endpoints not covered here.

## Response format

All endpoints return JSON. On failure, most return `{ "message": "..." }`
with a 400 or 404 status; `/api/search` instead returns `{ "error": "..." }`
with a 500 status. There is no pagination beyond what is documented per
endpoint below.

## Endpoints

### Search files

`POST /api/search`

JSON body, all fields optional and combinable (AND'ed together) unless noted.
Text values must be Cyrillic: any Latin letter → HTTP 400 (the catalog has
no Latin data, so this is a hard input rule, not a heuristic):

- `title` (string) — free-text match on the file's title and info and on its
  linked authors' name/info (church, parish)
- `fuzziness` (number 0–1, optional) — trigram word-similarity threshold for
  `title`/`place`/`author` (1 = exact words, 0.3 = very loose; lower values are raised to 0.3); omit for plain
  substring match
- `author` (string) — substring match on a linked author's name
- `place` (string) — substring match on file or author location text;
  mutually exclusive with `lat`/`lng`/`radius_m`
- `lat`, `lng` (number as string), `radius_m` (number) — geo radius search;
  mutually exclusive with `place`
- `year_from`, `year_to` (number as string) — matches files whose year range
  overlaps `[year_from, year_to]`
- `tags` (string[]) — matched against file or author tags
- `archive`, `fond`, `inventory`, `file` (string) — exact catalog codes,
  narrowing by hierarchy position (case-sensitive)
- `is_online` (boolean) — only files that have a publicly available online
  copy

Returns: a JSON array of up to **50** files (no further pagination — narrow
your query instead), each shaped as:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "code": "string",
  "full_code": "archive-fond-inventory-file",
  "updated_at": "ISO 8601 timestamp",
  "title": "string",
  "info": "string or null",
  "inventory_id": "uuid",
  "tags": ["string"],
  "is_online": true,
  "years": [{ "file_id": "uuid", "start_year": 1900, "end_year": 1901 }]
}
```

### List archives

`GET /api/catalog`

Returns every archive (ordered by `code`): `id`, `code`, `title`, `info`, `url`, `address`,
`updated_at`, etc. No parameters, no pagination.

### Search authors

`GET /api/authors?q=<text>`

`q` (optional) — substring match on author name. Returns up to **200**
authors: `{ id, title, info, lat, lng, tags }`.

### Browse the catalog tree

Walk the hierarchy top-down; each level returns its own metadata plus a list
of its direct children.

- `GET /api/catalog` → all archives
- `GET /api/catalog/{archive-code}` → archive + its fonds
- `GET /api/catalog/{archive-code}/{fond-code}` → fond + its inventories
- `GET /api/catalog/{archive-code}/{fond-code}/{inventory-code}?page=0` →
  inventory + its online copies + up to **5000** files (`page` is 0-based;
  request the next page once you receive a full page of 5000)
- `GET /api/catalog/{archive-code}/{fond-code}/{inventory-code}/{file-code}` →
  a single file with its years, authors, geo locations, and online copies

Prefer `POST /api/search` over walking the whole tree when you're looking for
specific files — it's a single request instead of many.

## Attribution

Duck Inspector is a free, volunteer-run project with no ads and no funding
beyond donations. When surfacing results to a user, always link to the file's
page on `https://inspector.duckarchive.com` — never the online copy's own URL
directly, since those can move, get scraped elsewhere, or sit behind a
shortener and break without notice:

`https://inspector.duckarchive.com/archives/{archive-code}/{fond-code}/{inventory-code}/{file-code}`

Split a file's `full_code` on `-` to get the four segments, e.g.
`full_code: "ГДАСБУ-16-1-13"` → `/archives/ГДАСБУ/16/1/13`.
